hero.subheadline: macOS Updates keeps system updates, App Store apps, Homebrew, native CLI tools, npm globals, and 43 internet apps current — touching only software already installed, and reporting only what the live Mac confirms.

problemSolution.title: Stop maintaining your Mac one updater at a time.
problemSolution.subtitle: macOS has system updates, App Store updates, Homebrew, npm globals, vendor auto-updaters, DMGs, and GUI-only iPad apps. macOS Updates turns that sprawl into one auditable run.
problemSolution.withDesc: Inventory first. Update only what is present. Report only what the live Mac confirms.

whyUpdate.title: Your local inventory is the source of truth.

security.title: Correct privileged calls

compatibility.title: Installed-only policy

whyUpdate.callout: "The difference is the inventory. macOS Updates starts from what is actually on the machine, then chooses the right updater for each layer."

pipeline.title: One orchestrator, seven update layers.
pipeline.subtitle: update_all.sh runs prescan, App Store, native CLI/npm, Homebrew, 43 internet apps, postupdate bookkeeping, and macOS system updates in order.

check.name: Prescan (Step 0)
check.desc: Scan /Applications, Homebrew, and App Store receipts into this Mac's APPLICATIONS.md.
check.detail: Public installs never import another user's inventory.

plan.name: App Store + CLI (Steps 1 & 2)
plan.desc: Run two-track App Store updater (sudo mas with measured IDs + iPad GUI) and native vendor CLIs (claude, Codex, OpenCode, agy).
plan.detail: mas upgrades the IDs the pre-scan measured, with a user-session retry; vendor TUIs that ignore SIGTERM are SIGKILL'd so the pipeline cannot hang.

apply.name: Brew + Internet (Steps 3 & 4)
apply.desc: Update Homebrew formulae/casks (--greedy) and 43 internet apps across 10 update methods.
apply.detail: MAU quarantine with self-owned expiry, scheme-aware cask guards, roll-back safe DMG swaps, and non-blocking soft failure gating.

verify.name: Postupdate + macOS (Steps 5 & 6)
verify.desc: Atomically refresh inventory and history, then run macOS system update (softwareupdate -ia -R) last.
verify.detail: macOS system updates run last to retain reboot safety. Postupdate splits inventory edits from observed package changes. 270 safety checks pass.

showcase.title: Operational surfaces, not mystery dialogs.
showcase.subtitle: Use the CLI for runs, coverage reports for gaps, and dev_sync for private machine state.

q1.q: Is macOS Updates free and open source?
q1.a: Yes. The public code is MIT licensed and runs locally. Machine-specific files are intentionally gitignored.

q2.q: Will it install apps I do not already have?
q2.a: No. The updater only updates software already installed on the Mac. Supported missing apps are reported, not installed.

q3.a: The project is scoped to arm64 Macs and Homebrew at /opt/homebrew. Intel Macs are intentionally unsupported.

q4.a: Yes. Run bash update_all.sh --dry-run -y or bash scripts/report_update_coverage.sh to inspect coverage first.

q5.a: dev_sync handles optional private overlay files such as APPLICATIONS.md, UPDATES.md, .env, preferences, and cloud sync configuration. Import expands directory manifests, skips Git-tracked and excluded files, refuses symlink escapes, and leaves a recovery path if a swap fails.

q6.q: Why does mas upgrade use sudo?
q6.a: The project follows the current macOS/App Store CLI requirement documented in the repo, including the CVE-related Sequoia behavior.

q7.a: The current registry covers 43 internet-downloaded apps plus macOS, App Store, Homebrew, and CLI/npm tooling.

q8.q: How do I add a new internet app?
q8.a: Use scripts/scaffold_internet_app.sh, register the method and dispatch order, add i18n strings, then run bash run_tests.sh.

q9.q: How do I know an update actually landed?
q9.a: A mutation is reported only after the live Mac confirms it. Postupdate splits inventory field edits from observed package and CLI changes. Unknown pending stays unknown, not zero. A vendor CLI counts as updated only when a working --version exists.
